headline: 9-year-old son spent $118,000 on YouTube ads for his Minecraft channel using company credit card
summary: The father had saved his company credit card to his Google account, which his son also used, leading to the massive bill over about three weeks for promoting gameplay videos.
details: A 9-year-old boy reportedly spent $118,000 on YouTube ad campaigns for his Minecraft and Roblox gameplay videos over three weeks. The charges were made to a company credit card his father had saved to his Google account, which the son also used.

The father, identified as Dave, explained in a video that he initially set up a small $20 promotion. His son then created his own campaigns, not understanding the $20 as a limit, as the credit card was automatically approved for every transaction without a set cap.

The incident led to Dave being called into a meeting with his company's management and finance department. He stated that he does not yet know if he will keep his job or be required to repay the substantial costs incurred.

Google's payment system stores methods in a profile tied to the account, shared across products like Google Ads. While Google Ads typically requires users to be over 18, the account belonged to the father. This echoes a 2014 FTC case where Google refunded parents for unauthorized in-app purchases by children.

To prevent future incidents, the family plans to remove all saved payment details, implement spending caps, and set up parental controls. The son's YouTube channel, "Mighty Mike Plays," which had around 24,000 subscribers, is currently paused until "real guard rails" are in place.
